facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah has been anxious all the time, and it got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Became deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school.

facts.heading: Taught for eleven years
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and I love it.

facts.heading: Rehearsing meeting in head
facts.content: Hannah rehearses in her head on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head

facts.heading: Rehearsing questions and thoughts
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say.
facts.evidence: I rehearse every possible question someone might ask and what I would say, then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Imagines being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines that people think she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth, that they gave the job to a nice year four teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Email about behaviour policy
facts.content: The email Hannah rewrote was about changing the behaviour policy.
facts.evidence: Change to the behaviour policy. It was too pergress.

facts.heading: Afraid of being seen as stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr Hargraves was kind
facts.content: Mr Hargraves has been kind to Hannah.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feels like she is lying
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr Hargraves.
facts.evidence: It makes it worse somehow, because I feel like I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Pretending to be capable
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is pretending to be capable.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feels like a child
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat most days.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a head teacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother was brilliant
facts.content: Hannah's mother was brilliant.
facts.evidence: She was brilliant.

facts.heading: Mother's hat remembered
facts.content: People still remember Hannah's mother's wonderful hat.
facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me saying what a wonderful hat she was.

facts.heading: Mother retired six years ago
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Compares everything to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to what her mother would have done better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother is supportive on surface
facts.content: Hannah's mother is supportive on the surface.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Feels like making a fuss
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is making a fuss to avoid telling her mother the extent of her feelings.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine. Then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Drinking coffee to cope
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day. This is happening since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term, I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: During the afternoons, Hannah's heart goes fast and her hands are shaky.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water due to physical symptoms.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day, just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice on feelings
facts.content: Ben suggested Hannah should just enjoy her feelings. Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben says this.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it. Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner's profession and reaction
facts.content: Ben is an engineer and thinks he can fix problems.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, he fix it.

facts.heading: Loss of friendships at school
facts.content: Hannah no longer has friends at school who have talked to her.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year 4 corridor with the others.

facts.heading: Lost company with promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company along with her promotion. She had not thought of it that way.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.

facts.heading: Missed classes and children
facts.content: Hannah missed her class and missed the daily moments where a child got something for the first time.
facts.evidence: I missed my class too. The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Promotion decision and tears
facts.content: Hannah said yes to the promotion because she couldn't say no to her. She cried after going home.
facts.evidence: I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her. The hat. Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Tears expressed fear
facts.content: The tears were about fear and the fear of never getting to go back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays while walking in the lakes.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays, we went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Difference during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of her and she was just walking while Ben carried the sandwiches.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking. Ben carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Pre-term breakdown
facts.content: The week before a term started, Hannah was a wreck again. She could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before a term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A cheer of laughing. A good email. It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Felt silly bragging to self
facts.content: Hannah felt silly when writing down positive events. She felt like she was bragging to herself in a notebook.
facts.evidence: As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well was not the same as bragging. It just felt that way.

facts.heading: Wants to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud. She envisions not rehearsing meetings and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Mmm, walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first, sending an email once.

facts.heading: Wants evening calm time
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feelings about goals
facts.content: Hannah felt light and a bit tearful when stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: First time sharing bad news
facts.content: This is the first time Hannah has told anyone how bad her situation is. She has not told Ben about the 4AM issue.
facts.evidence: That's the first time I've told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about the 4AM.

facts.heading: Scared to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben about the 4AM issue. She worries he would hear she didn't say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be heard that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Quiet time for sharing
facts.content: Hannah plans to try telling someone this week if she chooses a quiet moment. She will put the notebook by the kettle.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Plans to share with Ben
facts.content: Hannah plans to talk to Ben over breakfast on Saturday morning. She expects him to be in a good mood then.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? He is always in a good mood then.
